doc.title: yq: wildcard (`.["a*"]`, `.a*`) and integer (`.[1]`, `has(1)`) mapping-key traversal are not implemented
doc.body:
## Symptom

Real yq routes every mapping-key lookup through `matchKey` (`pkg/yqlib/matchKeyString.go`,
v4.53.3) -- a byte-level glob where `*` is zero or more bytes and `?` exactly one -- and
matches a key by its *text*, so an integer index also finds an `!!int` key. Captured live,
`-o=json -I0`, on `abc: 1\nabd: 2\nx: 3\n1: y\n`:

| filter                      | yq                                    | succinctly                              |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `.["ab*"]`                  | `1` `2`                               | `null`                                  |
| `.ab*`                      | `1` `2`                               | parse error                             |
| `[.["a?c"]]`                | `[1]`                                 | `[null]`                                |
| `[.["*"]] \| length`        | `4`                                   | `1`                                     |
| `.ab* = 9`                  | `{"abc":9,"abd":9,...}`               | parse error                             |
| `del(.["ab*"])`             | `{"x":3,"1":"y"}`                     | unchanged                               |
| `.[1]`                      | `"y"`                                 | `null`                                  |
| `has(1)`                    | `true`                                | `false`                                 |
| `.[1] = "z"`                | `{...,"1":"z"}`                       | `Cannot index object with number`       |
| `has("ab*")`                | `false`                               | `false` (`has` is exact -- agrees)      |
| `.[] \| select(key == "ab*")` | `1` `2`                             | `1` `2` (#2785's `==` already matches)  |

Two quirks worth capturing before implementing, both live on v4.53.3: `del(.["1"])` and
`del(.[1])` on the `1: y` member are **no-ops** (`.["1"]` reads it fine), and `.["x*y"]`
on no match is `null`, not empty.

## Where the code is

- The matcher already exists: `glob::yq_match_key` (`src/jq/glob.rs`, #2785) is the
  byte-for-byte port used by `==`; traversal needs the same function at the key-lookup
  sites (`find_cursor`/`DocumentFields::get` and the `.[n]`-on-object arm), plus a parser
  change for the bare `.ab*` spelling.
- Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under #2785's residuals.

Split out of #2785.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (`2581b17c9`):** still reproduces on `main` and, except the `select(key == "ab*")` row (now `1 2` via the text `==`), identically on PR #2804's branch binary. Re-captured on `abc: 1 / abd: 2 / x: 3 / 1: y` (`-o=json -I0`, yq v4.53.3 vs `main`):

| filter | yq | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `.["ab*"]`, `.ab*`, `."ab*"` | `1` `2` | `null` / parse error / `null` |
| `[.["*"]] \| length`, `.*` | `4`, `1 2 3 "y"` | `1`, parse error |
| `.a?c`, `.*c`, `.a**`, `.ab*?` | `1`, `1`, `1 2`, `1 2` | parse errors |
| `.ab?` | `null` (trailing `?` is jq's optional, not a wildcard) | `null` (agrees) |
| `.a*b`, `.["x*y"]`, `[.["x*y"]]` | `null`, `null`, `[null]` | parse error, `null`, `[null]` |
| `.["ab*"] \| key`, `.["ab*"] \| path` | `"abc" "abd"`, `["abc"] ["abd"]` | `"ab*"`, `["ab*"]` |
| `.ab* = 9`, `.["*"] = 0`, `.["ab*"] \|= . + 10`, `.["ab*"] += 10` | every match written | parse error / literal `"*"`/`"ab*"` key created |
| `.["zz*"] = 5`, `.["zz*"] \|= 7` (no match) | literal key `zz*` created | same (agrees) |
| `del(.["ab*"])` | `{"x":3,"1":"y"}` | unchanged |
| `.[1]`, `.[1]?`, `.1`, `has(1)` | `"y"`, `"y"`, `"y"`, `true` | `null`, `null`, parse error, `false` |
| `.[1] = "z"` | `1:` member updated | `Cannot index object with number` |
| `.[1] = "z"` on `{}` / on `null` | `{"1":"z"}` (key tagged `!!int`) / `[null,"z"]` | — |
| `.[1.5]`, `.[1.50]`, `.[01]`, `.[true]`, `.[null]` on `1.5: w / 1: x / true: t / null: z` | `"w"`, `null`, `null`, `"t"`, `"z"` | `null`, `null`, `null`, `Cannot index object with boolean`, `Cannot index object with null` |
| `has("ab*")`, `has(01)`, `has(null)` on `null: z` | `false`, `false`, `true` | `false`, `false`, `false` |
| `del(.["1"])`, `del(.[1])`, `del(.1)`, `del(."1")` on `1: y` | all **no-ops** | `del(.["1"])` deletes |
| `del(.true)`, `del(.null)` on `true: t / null: n` | both delete | — |
| `.["1"]` on a sequence `[a, b]` | `"b"` (string index parsed as int) | `Cannot index array with string "1"` |
| `.["*"]` on a sequence | `cannot index array with '*' (strconv.ParseInt...)` | — |
| `pick(.["ab*"])` | `{}` | `pick: argument must be an array of keys` |
| `.["ab*"] \| parent \| keys` | `["abc","abd","x",1]` twice | nothing |

The rule, from `operator_traverse_path.go`/`matchKeyString.go`/`operator_has.go` (v4.53.3, read alongside the probes): a mapping lookup compares the **index node's `.Value` text** against each key's `.Value` text with `matchKey` (`*` = zero or more bytes, `?` = exactly one, `""` matches only `""`, `"*"` matches all); every match is returned in document order (`orderedmap`, so a duplicated key still yields its last value); no match and not read-only → a `null` member is auto-created under the literal pattern (that is the `.["zz*"] = 5` row and the `.["x*y"]` → `null` row). `.[1.50]`/`.[01]` miss because the *literal's* text is `1.50`/`01`. `has` is exact text equality on mappings (no glob); on sequences it is `len > n` only for an `!!int` argument. The `del` no-op on an int-spelled key is real yq's own bug (a `!!bool`/`!!null` key deletes fine).

**Root cause / mechanism:** every succinctly lookup is exact and string-only. Reads: `Expr::Field` arm and `index_one_generic` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs` call `DocumentFields::find_cursor(name)` (`src/jq/document.rs`, YAML impl `YamlFields::find_cursor_at_depth` in `src/yaml/light.rs`, which also carries the merge-key fallback #1318); the eager evaluator's `index_object_by_name`/`index_one` in `src/jq/eval.rs`; a numeric index on an object raises `cannot_index` before any lookup. Writes: `set_path`/`set_path_steps`/`update_path`/`update_path_steps`/`delete_at_path` (`eval.rs`) walk an `OwnedValue::Object(IndexMap<String,_>)` by exact key; the `Expr::Index` arm autovivifies an *array* and errors on an object. `has` (`DocumentFields::contains` via `key_display_string`) is already text-exact and agrees except for a non-string argument. The parser (`src/jq/parser.rs`, `ParserMode::Yq`) has no bare-field spelling that admits `*`, an embedded `?`, or a leading digit. The matcher itself exists on PR #2804: `glob::yq_match_key` (`src/jq/glob.rs`), a byte-for-byte port of `deepMatch`.

**Plan:** (after PR #2804 lands — it brings `glob::yq_match_key` and the text `==`)
1. **Parser, `ParserMode::Yq` only**: extend the bare-field lexeme so `.ab*`, `.*`, `.**`, `.a*c`, `.*c`, `.a?c` and `.1` parse as `Expr::Field` with the raw text; `?` is a wildcard only when *followed by* another field byte, a trailing `?` stays `Expr::Optional` (`.ab?` → optional, `.ab*?` → wildcard then optional — both captured above). jq mode unchanged (`jq` rejects `.ab*`). Add parser unit tests for each spelling, plus `.a*.b` and `.a*[0]` chains.
2. **Read lookups**: add `DocumentFields::find_cursors_matching(pattern) -> Result<Vec<Cursor>, EvalError>` (default: exact `find_cursor` when the pattern has no `*`/`?`, so JSON/jq mode pays nothing) with a YAML implementation that walks the fields once, keeps the last cursor per distinct matched key text (yq's `orderedmap` semantics), and reuses `merge_fallback` for the no-match case. Route `Expr::Field` and `index_one_generic`'s `String` arm through it when `S::TAG == Yq`; a numeric/bool/null index on an object in yq mode becomes a text lookup (`numeric_display_string` of the literal — `1.50` stays `1.50`), never the `cannot_index` error. Results are `GenericResult::Many` cursors when >1, `OneCursor` when 1, and the existing `yq_absent_key_read_is_empty`/`Owned(Null)` split when 0 (keep #2470's read-only rule exactly; `[.["x*y"]]` → `[null]`). Bypass the large-object key table (#1514, `document.rs`) for a pattern with a wildcard; exact int lookups can use it with the text. Mirror in `eval.rs` `index_object_by_name`/`index_one` for the eager evaluator (both evaluators — the #2226 trap).
3. **Writes**: in `set_path_steps`/`update_path_steps`/`delete_at_path` (`eval.rs`) and whatever `yq_runner.rs` DOM route feeds them, a yq-mode `Field`/`Index` step on an object resolves to every key whose text matches; fan the write/update out over all of them (`.["ab*"] |= . + 10` writes both, and `path`/`key` inside the update see the concrete key); zero matches → create the literal key (`zz*`), matching yq. `.[1] = "z"` on an object updates `1:`; on `{}` creates `1:`; on `null` autovivifies an array (unchanged). Decide `del(.["1"])`/`del(.[1])` on an int-spelled key: yq's no-op discards a write, which is ADR-0018 rule 4(b) territory — recommended: keep deleting, record the divergence in limitations.md with the captured no-op rows.
4. **`has`**: on a mapping, compare `has`'s argument by text for any scalar (`has(null)` → `true` on a `null:` key, `has(1)` → `true` on `1:`); on a sequence, `has("1")` stays `false` (only `!!int` counts). `.["1"]` on a *sequence* parses the string as an index in yq (`"b"` above) — same PR or record; it is the mirror of the int-on-mapping rule.
5. **Path register / `key` after a wildcard**: falls out of step 2 because each match is a real cursor (`cursor_slot` sees the concrete key); pin `.["ab*"] | key`, `| path`, `| parent | keys`. `pick(.["ab*"])` → `{}` is a yq oddity of its own; record, do not implement.
6. Tests: goldens (`scripts/sync-yq-golden.sh`) for the read table, the write table and the `has`/`del` rows; `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` pins for the parser spellings, the fan-out on the cursor path and through a bridge (`[.["ab*"]]`, `.["ab*"] as $v | $v`, `.abc = 5 | .["ab*"]` → `5 2`), duplicate keys (`a: 1 / a: 2 / ab: 3` → `.["a*"]` is `2 3`), the read-only/absent split, and YAML-output shapes (a `Many` result loses the `CommentTree` — #1349 — so a comment/anchor-bearing document under `.ab*` must be pinned as it actually prints, not as yq prints it, and recorded). Perf: `dev bench yq` interleaved on both chips for `.name` on the 100k-key mapping (the `#1514` table path must stay on the exact route) and `.["a*"]` on the same.
7. Docs: limitations.md — close the `#2800` bullets under #2785's key-node entry and `#2785`'s `==` entry, add the `del`-no-op and `pick` quirks with the captured rows; `docs/reference/yq-language.md` traversal section (wildcards, int index on mappings, `has` text rule); CLAUDE.md yq section gets one paragraph.

**Risks / open questions:**
- A wildcard write path fans out inside `set_path`/`update_path`, which are already the most intricate functions in `eval.rs` (`#1429`'s one-component-at-a-time walk); keep the fan-out as a new step kind rather than special-casing each arm, and re-run the depth-guard tests after any struct widening.
- The `?`-inside-a-field lexer rule interacts with `.a?.b` (optional then field) — `.a?c` is a wildcard only because `c` is a field byte; `.a?.b` must remain optional-then-field. Pin both.
- Text-matching an int index means `.[0]` on a mapping with a `0:` key now returns it in yq mode — correct per yq, but it changes a `null` into a value; grep the yq goldens for `.[0]` on mappings before flipping.
- `Many` results lose comments/anchors on YAML output (#1349) — a fidelity cap this PR inherits, not creates.
- The large-object hash lookup (#1514) must not be consulted with a glob; measure that the exact path did not regress.

**Dependencies / related:** PR #2804/#2785 (matcher + text `==`, land first); #2801 (path register — overlapping scope: #2801 will also deliver this issue's integer-index lookup and wildcard key matcher, so most of the traversal work is done there and only the `has()` and delete sites would remain here); #2470/#2482 (absent-key and scalar-target rules the new lookup must preserve); #1318 (merge-key fallback in `find_cursor`); #1514 (key table); #1349 (`Many` loses `CommentTree`); #2226 (shared-mode fix needs both evaluators).

**Class:** Opus — a parser change plus the same rule at every read, write, delete and `has` site across both evaluators and the DOM write walker, a semantics matrix re-derived from the reference source with several quirks to adjudicate under ADR-0018 (the `del` no-op, `pick`, string index on sequences), a `Many`-result fidelity cap to record, and a perf gate on the exact-lookup hot path. No new representation or ADR, so not Fable; far too many sites and forks for Sonnet.

edit.from: #2801 (path register — independent, but `setpath([1]; v)` on a mapping needs this issue's int-index lookup)
edit.to: #2801 (path register — overlapping scope: #2801 will also deliver this issue's integer-index lookup and wildcard key matcher, so most of the traversal work is done there and only the `has()` and delete sites would remain here)

doc.title: yq: `==`/`!=` never match a container, and unique/group_by key on scalar text -- succinctly answers structurally
doc.body:
## Symptom

#2785 adopted real yq's *scalar* `==`/`!=` rule (text, with `*`/`?` wildcards on the right
operand -- `eval::yq_scalar_text_eq`). Two neighbouring halves of the same `isEquals`
(`pkg/yqlib/operator_equals.go`, v4.53.3) are still answered jq's way. Captured live,
`-o=json -I0`, on `l: [1]\nm: {x: 1}\na: 1\nb: "1"\n`:

| filter                              | yq       | succinctly   |
|-------------------------------------|----------|--------------|
| `[1] == [1]`                        | `false`  | `true`       |
| `.l == .l`, `. == .`                | `false`  | `true`       |
| `{} == {}`, `.m == {"x": 1}`        | `false`  | `true`       |
| `[1] != [1]`                        | `true`   | `false`      |
| `[.a, .b] \| unique`                | `[1]`    | `[1, "1"]`   |
| `[1, "1", 01] \| unique`            | `[1, 1]` | `[1, "1"]`   |
| `[.a, .b] \| group_by(.) \| length` | `1`      | `2`          |
| `[.b, .a] \| sort`                  | `["1", 1]` | `[1, "1"]` |

Real yq's `isEquals` answers `false` unless the left operand is `!!null` (then: right is
`!!null`) or both operands are scalar nodes -- an array or object pairing is never equal,
`. == .` included. `unique`/`unique_by`/`group_by` key their ordered map on the node's
`.Value` text (`getUniqueKeyValue`, `processIntoGroups`), so `1` and `"1"` dedup together
there -- *without* the wildcard, which is why #2785 kept the text rule out of
`owned_value_eq` (#950's shared dedup definition): a glob is neither symmetric nor
transitive and cannot key a map. `sort`'s comparator (`operator_sort.go`) is typed for
null/bool/number pairs and falls back to `strings.Compare` on the text for anything else,
which is how `"1"` sorts before `1` (equal text, stable order).

## Where the code is

- `eval::yq_scalar_text_eq` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) returns `None` for any container operand so
  the structural rule decides; the container half is a one-line change there once the
  fidelity call is made (ADR-0018: nothing here is a rule-4 exception, but `[1] == [1]`
  being `false` is a large behavioural change for `select`-heavy scripts).
- `value::owned_value_eq` is what `unique`/`unique_by`/`group_by`/`contains`/array `-`
  consume; the dedup half wants a text-key beside it, not a change to it.
- Pinned as today's answers by `yq_text_equality_2785::the_rest_of_the_equality_family_is_unchanged_2785`
  (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`) and recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.

Split out of #2785, which needed only the scalar rule to unblock typed key nodes.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (`2581b17c9`):** still reproduces, identically on `main` and on PR #2804's branch binary (the PR's `yq_scalar_text_eq` returns `None` for any container, exactly as the issue says). Every row of the issue's table re-captured with `-o=json -I0` on `l: [1] / m: {x: 1} / a: 1 / b: "1"`, plus the rows that pin the *shape* of the fix (yq v4.53.3 first, `main` second):

| filter | yq | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `[.l == .l, . == ., .l == [1], [1] == .l]` | `[false,false,false,false]` | `[true,true,true,true]` |
| `[{} == {}, .m == {"x": 1}, .o == {}, .e == []]` | all `false` | all `true` |
| `[1] != [1]`, `[{} != {}]` | `true` | `false` |
| `[.l == null, null == .l, .e == null]` | `false` | `false` (agrees) |
| `[.a, .b] \| unique`, `[.a, .b] \| unique_by(.)` | `[1]` | `[1,"1"]` |
| `[1, "1", 01] \| unique` | `[1,1]` | `[1,"1"]` |
| `["1.0", 1.0] \| unique` | `["1.0"]` | `[1.0,"1.0"]` |
| `[1, [1], "1"] \| unique` | `[1,[1]]` | `[1,"1",[1]]` |
| `[[1],[2]] \| unique` | `[[1],[2]]` | `[[1],[2]]` |
| `[[1],[2]] \| group_by(.) \| length` | `1` | `2` |
| `[3,1,2,1] \| unique` | `[3,1,2]` | `[1,2,3]` |
| `[3,1,2,1] \| group_by(.)` | `[[3],[1,1],[2]]` | `[[1,1],[2],[3]]` |
| `["abc", "a*"] \| unique` | `["abc","a*"]` | `["a*","abc"]` |
| `[.b, .a] \| sort` | `["1",1]` | `[1,"1"]` |
| `[2, "10", 3] \| sort` | `["10",2,3]` | `[2,3,"10"]` |
| `[[1,2],1,"x",null,true] \| sort` | `[null,true,[1,2],1,"x"]` | `[null,true,1,"x",[1,2]]` |
| `[[3],[1],[2]] \| sort` | `[[3],[1],[2]]` | `[[1],[2],[3]]` |
| `[1, true, "true", null, "null", 1.0, "1.0"] \| unique` | `[1,true,null,1.0]` | `[null,true,1,1.0,"1.0","null","true"]` |

Two things the issue does not say, both load-bearing for the plan (read from the v4.53.3 sources `operator_unique.go`, `operator_group_by.go`, `operator_sort.go`, saved alongside these probes):

- **`unique`/`unique_by`/`group_by` do not sort in yq** — they are an `orderedmap` keyed on text, so output is first-occurrence order (`[3,1,2,1] | unique` → `[3,1,2]`). succinctly sorts first (jq's definition). This ordering divergence is unrecorded anywhere in limitations.md and cannot be separated from the text-key change (the current sort-then-`dedup_by`-adjacent implementation cannot key on text at all), so it is in scope.
- **The dedup key differs between `unique` and `group_by`.** `getUniqueKeyValue`: a scalar's `.Value`; a container's *YAML encoding* (`encodeToString(..., YamlFormat)`), so `[[1],[2]]` stay distinct but a flow `[1]` and a block `- 1` may not. `processIntoGroups` (`group_by`): `.Value` only, so **every container keys to `""`** and `[[1],[2]] | group_by(.)` is one group. A missing key result keys as the text `null`.
- `sort`'s comparator (`sortableNodeArray.compare`) is typed only for null/bool/`!!int`×`!!int`/int-or-float pairs/timestamps and otherwise `strings.Compare(lhs.Value, rhs.Value)`; a container's `.Value` is `""`, so containers sort between bools and everything else. Stable sort, so equal text keeps input order (`["1", 1]`).

**Root cause / mechanism:** `eval::apply_compare_op` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) is the single `==`/`!=` definition for all evaluators; PR #2804's `yq_scalar_text_eq` sits in front of it and declines containers. `value::owned_value_eq` (#950's one shared definition) is consumed by `builtin_unique`/`builtin_unique_by`/`builtin_group_by` (`eval.rs`, after `items.sort_by(compare_values)`), by the generic evaluator's `Sort | SortBy | Unique | UniqueBy` arm (`sort_family_array_generic` + `sort_keyed_elements`, `src/jq/eval_generic.rs`), and by `contains`/`inside`/array `-`/`index`/`IN` — the last group is *not* in scope (yq's `contains` and `-` are their own operators; `[.a, .b] - [.b]` already agrees). `compare_values` (`eval.rs`) is jq's type-ranked ordering and is what `sort`/`sort_by`/`min`/`max` use in both evaluators.

**Plan:** three PRs under this issue, in this order, each with its own oracle table.
1. **Container `==`/`!=`** (after PR #2804 merges): in `eval::yq_scalar_text_eq`, when `S::TAG == Yq` and either operand is `Array`/`Object`, return `Some(false)` for `Eq` / `Some(true)` for `Ne` (the `!!null`-lhs branch already comes first and already answers `false`). Flip the container rows pinned by `yq_text_equality_2785::the_rest_of_the_equality_family_is_unchanged_2785` (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`). Check that nothing internal routes through `apply_compare_op` for structural equality: the alias-identity equal-value rule (`jq::alias_identity`), `owned_value_eq`'s callers, `//` and `select` all use their own predicates — confirm by grep, then pin `. as $d | [.[] | select(. == $d.l)]` → `[]`, `with_entries(select(.value == [1])) | keys` → `[]`, `(.l == .l) | not` → `true` (all captured above).
2. **Dedup keys + first-occurrence order**: add a yq-mode key function beside `owned_value_eq` (not inside it — the wildcard-free text key is what yq uses, and a glob cannot key a map): `yq_unique_key(&OwnedValue) -> String` = scalar text (`owned_to_string`, same renderer `yq_scalar_text` uses so `==` and `unique` agree) or, for containers, the `@yaml`-style encoding (reuse `owned_to_yaml_at_depth`/the flow emitter; note #1183 says that emitter already diverges from yq, so pin container-dedup cases at the level of "equal encodings dedup, different ones don't" rather than exact bytes); and `yq_group_key` = scalar text or `""` for a container. In both `eval.rs` (`builtin_unique`, `builtin_unique_by`, `builtin_group_by`) and `eval_generic.rs` (`sort_family_array_generic`'s dedup closure — `Unique`/`UniqueBy` currently ride the `Sort` path; split them so yq mode skips `sort_keyed_elements` and keeps document order), under `S::TAG == Yq`: insertion-ordered `IndexMap<String, _>` keyed on the text, no sort. jq mode unchanged. `unique_by(f)`/`group_by(f)` with an empty `f` result key as `"null"`.
3. **`sort`/`sort_by` comparator**: a yq-mode `yq_compare_values` beside `compare_values` implementing `compare` above (null < bool < everything; bool by truthiness; `(Int, Int)` numeric; int/float mix by f64; else `strings.Compare` on the `.Value` text, `""` for containers; timestamps only when both are `!!timestamp`, which succinctly does not type — record that gap), used by `builtin_sort`/`builtin_sort_by` and `sort_keyed_elements` when `S::TAG == Yq`; stable sort already. `min`/`max`/`min_by`/`max_by` use `compare_values` too — check yq's `operator_min_max.go` before touching them (not probed here).
4. Tests: goldens (`scripts/sync-yq-golden.sh`) for each table above; `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` pins per PR including the yq-only quirks (`group_by` collapsing containers, `["abc","a*"] | unique` keeping both — no glob in dedup — and `[1, "1", 01] | unique` → `[1,1]` which needs #2802 to print `01`'s text; until then pin `length == 2`). A property test: for arrays of scalars, `unique | length` equals the number of distinct `tostring` texts and the output is a subsequence of the input. Both evaluators: run each pin through a shape that stays on the cursor path (`.arr | unique`) and one that bridges (`[.[] | .x] | unique`), the two-evaluator trap from #2226.
5. Docs: limitations.md — replace the `#2799` bullet under the `#2785` `==` entry with resolved rows; add the `group_by`-collapses-containers and style-dependent container `unique` key as recorded yq quirks; `docs/reference/yq-language.md` comparison/dedup section; CLAUDE.md's `unique`/`sort` mentions if any state jq ordering for yq mode.

**Risks / open questions:**
- `[1] == [1]` → `false` and `. == .` → `false` will change `select`-heavy scripts; it is exact fidelity (`isEquals`, source read), no rule-4 condition applies, so ADR-0018 says reproduce — but the release note must be explicit.
- Unique's container key is the *encoded YAML* including style; matching that byte-for-byte is out of reach until #1183/#1076 (the `@yaml` emitter) are fixed — pin the equivalence classes, not the bytes, and record the style-sensitivity.
- `[1, "1", 01] | unique` is `[1,1]` in yq: `"1"` collapses into `1` (same text) but `01` does not (text `01`, printed as `1` by `-o=json`). A filter literal `01` here is a `NumberLiteral` carrying `"01"`, so the text key should reproduce that; a *document* `01` will not until #2802 (its text is gone at `to_owned`) — pin the literal case exactly, record the document case as a #2802 residual, do not block on it.
- Perf: the yq-mode `unique` moves from sort+adjacent-dedup (O(n log n), no allocation per element) to a text-keyed map (one `String` per element). Measure `dev bench yq` on a 1M-element `unique` on both chips, interleaved; a hash of the text without materializing the `String` (hash `owned_to_string`'s bytes into a `HashSet<u64>` + collision check) is the mitigation if it shows.
- `sort_by` on a mapping (#2064) and the path-tracked error wording (#1998) touch the same functions; coordinate rather than conflict.

**Dependencies / related:** PR #2804/#2785 (the scalar rule this extends; land first); #2802 (spellings — overlapping scope: #2802 will also deliver the key and compare text rules below, so only the first-occurrence ordering and the `sort` comparator would remain here); #950 (shared dedup definition), #1183/#1076 (`@yaml` emitter divergences that cap container-key fidelity), #2064, #1998, #2068 (a prior 4x `sort`/`unique` regression on large YAML — the perf gate here is not optional).

**Class:** Opus — three semantic rules re-derived from the reference source across both evaluators (`eval.rs` and `eval_generic.rs`), a fork the implementer must resolve under ADR-0018 with a large blast radius (`[1] == [1]` false), an unrecorded ordering divergence discovered during triage that widens the scope, a container-key rule that can only be matched up to an equivalence class, and an interleaved two-architecture A/B on the dedup builtins that have regressed 4x before (#2068). No new representation or ADR, so not Fable.

comments.body:
Extra rows from #3069's investigation (agent `Agatha`). They look like the same text-keyed `unique`/`group_by` mechanism, reached through NaN. Captured live against yq v4.53.3, `-o=json -I=0`, on `a: [.nan]\nb: [.nan]\nc: [1]\nn: .nan\n`:

| filter                           | yq  | succinctly |
|----------------------------------|-----|------------|
| `[.n,.n] \| unique \| length`      | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.a] \| unique \| length`      | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.b] \| unique \| length`      | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.c] \| unique \| length`      | `2` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.a] \| unique_by(.) \| length` | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.a] \| group_by(.) \| length`  | `1` | `2`        |

Two sequences holding NaN merge in yq, but `[.nan]` and `[1]` do not. So the key is not simply a sequence node's empty `.Value`. Worth pinning whatever key `getUniqueKeyValue` actually builds for a sequence when this issue is picked up. `==` itself agrees in both (`.a == .a` is `false`), and #3069 leaves yq mode unchanged.

- `sort`'s comparator (`sortableNodeArray.compare`) is typed only for null/bool/`!!int`×`!!int`/int-or-float pairs/timestamps and otherwise `strings.Compare(lhs.Value, rhs.Value)`; a container's `.Value` is `""`, so containers sort between bools and everything else. Stable sort, so equal text keeps input order (`["1", 1]`).

**Root cause / mechanism:** `eval::apply_compare_op` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) is the single `==`/`!=` definition for all evaluators; PR #2804's `yq_scalar_text_eq` sits in front of it and declines containers. `value::owned_value_eq` (#950's one shared definition) is consumed by `builtin_unique`/`builtin_unique_by`/`builtin_group_by` (`eval.rs`, after `items.sort_by(compare_values)`), by the generic evaluator's `Sort | SortBy | Unique | UniqueBy` arm (`sort_family_array_generic` + `sort_keyed_elements`, `src/jq/eval_generic.rs`), and by `contains`/`inside`/array `-`/`index`/`IN` — the last group is *not* in scope (yq's `contains` and `-` are their own operators; `[.a, .b] - [.b]` already agrees). `compare_values` (`eval.rs`) is jq's type-ranked ordering and is what `sort`/`sort_by`/`min`/`max` use in both evaluators.

**Plan:** three PRs under this issue, in this order, each with its own oracle table.
1. **Container `==`/`!=`** (after PR #2804 merges): in `eval::yq_scalar_text_eq`, when `S::TAG == Yq` and either operand is `Array`/`Object`, return `Some(false)` for `Eq` / `Some(true)` for `Ne` (the `!!null`-lhs branch already comes first and already answers `false`). Flip the container rows pinned by `yq_text_equality_2785::the_rest_of_the_equality_family_is_unchanged_2785` (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`). Check that nothing internal routes through `apply_compare_op` for structural equality: the alias-identity equal-value rule (`jq::alias_identity`), `owned_value_eq`'s callers, `//` and `select` all use their own predicates — confirm by grep, then pin `. as $d | [.[] | select(. == $d.l)]` → `[]`, `with_entries(select(.value == [1])) | keys` → `[]`, `(.l == .l) | not` → `true` (all captured above).
2. **Dedup keys + first-occurrence order**: add a yq-mode key function beside `owned_value_eq` (not inside it — the wildcard-free text key is what yq uses, and a glob cannot key a map): `yq_unique_key(&OwnedValue) -> String` = scalar text (`owned_to_string`, same renderer `yq_scalar_text` uses so `==` and `unique` agree) or, for containers, the `@yaml`-style encoding (reuse `owned_to_yaml_at_depth`/the flow emitter; note #1183 says that emitter already diverges from yq, so pin container-dedup cases at the level of "equal encodings dedup, different ones don't" rather than exact bytes); and `yq_group_key` = scalar text or `""` for a container. In both `eval.rs` (`builtin_unique`, `builtin_unique_by`, `builtin_group_by`) and `eval_generic.rs` (`sort_family_array_generic`'s dedup closure — `Unique`/`UniqueBy` currently ride the `Sort` path; split them so yq mode skips `sort_keyed_elements` and keeps document order), under `S::TAG == Yq`: insertion-ordered `IndexMap<String, _>` keyed on the text, no sort. jq mode unchanged. `unique_by(f)`/`group_by(f)` with an empty `f` result key as `"null"`.
3. **`sort`/`sort_by` comparator**: a yq-mode `yq_compare_values` beside `compare_values` implementing `compare` above (null < bool < everything; bool by truthiness; `(Int, Int)` numeric; int/float mix by f64; else `strings.Compare` on the `.Value` text, `""` for containers; timestamps only when both are `!!timestamp`, which succinctly does not type — record that gap), used by `builtin_sort`/`builtin_sort_by` and `sort_keyed_elements` when `S::TAG == Yq`; stable sort already. `min`/`max`/`min_by`/`max_by` use `compare_values` too — check yq's `operator_min_max.go` before touching them (not probed here).
4. Tests: goldens (`scripts/sync-yq-golden.sh`) for each table above; `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` pins per PR including the yq-only quirks (`group_by` collapsing containers, `["abc","a*"] | unique` keeping both — no glob in dedup — and `[1, "1", 01] | unique` → `[1,1]` which needs #2802 to print `01`'s text; until then pin `length == 2`). A property test: for arrays of scalars, `unique | length` equals the number of distinct `tostring` texts and the output is a subsequence of the input. Both evaluators: run each pin through a shape that stays on the cursor path (`.arr | unique`) and one that bridges (`[.[] | .x] | unique`), the two-evaluator trap from #2226.
5. Docs: limitations.md — replace the `#2799` bullet under the `#2785` `==` entry with resolved rows; add the `group_by`-collapses-containers and style-dependent container `unique` key as recorded yq quirks; `docs/reference/yq-language.md` comparison/dedup section; CLAUDE.md's `unique`/`sort` mentions if any state jq ordering for yq mode.

**Risks / open questions:**
- `[1] == [1]` → `false` and `. == .` → `false` will change `select`-heavy scripts; it is exact fidelity (`isEquals`, source read), no rule-4 condition applies, so ADR-0018 says reproduce — but the release note must be explicit.
- Unique's container key is the *encoded YAML* including style; matching that byte-for-byte is out of reach until #1183/#1076 (the `@yaml` emitter) are fixed — pin the equivalence classes, not the bytes, and record the style-sensitivity.
- `[1, "1", 01] | unique` is `[1,1]` in yq: `"1"` collapses into `1` (same text) but `01` does not (text `01`, printed as `1` by `-o=json`). A filter literal `01` here is a `NumberLiteral` carrying `"01"`, so the text key should reproduce that; a *document* `01` will not until #2802 (its text is gone at `to_owned`) — pin the literal case exactly, record the document case as a #2802 residual, do not block on it.
- Perf: the yq-mode `unique` moves from sort+adjacent-dedup (O(n log n), no allocation per element) to a text-keyed map (one `String` per element). Measure `dev bench yq` on a 1M-element `unique` on both chips, interleaved; a hash of the text without materializing the `String` (hash `owned_to_string`'s bytes into a `HashSet<u64>` + collision check) is the mitigation if it shows.
- `sort_by` on a mapping (#2064) and the path-tracked error wording (#1998) touch the same functions; coordinate rather than conflict.

**Dependencies / related:** PR #2804/#2785 (the scalar rule this extends; land first); #2802 (spellings — landed: it also delivered the key and compare text rules below, so only the first-occurrence ordering and the `sort` comparator remain here); #950 (shared dedup definition), #1183/#1076 (`@yaml` emitter divergences that cap container-key fidelity), #2064, #1998, #2068 (a prior 4x `sort`/`unique` regression on large YAML — the perf gate here is not optional).

**Class:** Opus — three semantic rules re-derived from the reference source across both evaluators (`eval.rs` and `eval_generic.rs`), a fork the implementer must resolve under ADR-0018 with a large blast radius (`[1] == [1]` false), an unrecorded ordering divergence discovered during triage that widens the scope, a container-key rule that can only be matched up to an equivalence class, and an interleaved two-architecture A/B on the dedup builtins that have regressed 4x before (#2068). No new representation or ADR, so not Fable.

comments.body:
Extra rows from #3069's investigation (agent `Agatha`). They look like the same text-keyed `unique`/`group_by` mechanism, reached through NaN. Captured live against yq v4.53.3, `-o=json -I=0`, on `a: [.nan]\nb: [.nan]\nc: [1]\nn: .nan\n`:

| filter                           | yq  | succinctly |
|----------------------------------|-----|------------|
| `[.n,.n] \| unique \| length`      | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.a] \| unique \| length`      | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.b] \| unique \| length`      | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.c] \| unique \| length`      | `2` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.a] \| unique_by(.) \| length` | `1` | `2`        |
| `[.a,.a] \| group_by(.) \| length`  | `1` | `2`        |

Two sequences holding NaN merge in yq, but `[.nan]` and `[1]` do not. So the key is not simply a sequence node's empty `.Value`. Worth pinning whatever key `getUniqueKeyValue` actually builds for a sequence when this issue is picked up. `==` itself agrees in both (`.a == .a` is `false`), and #3069 leaves yq mode unchanged.
